title: Mantle Object: The Nobel Prize in Literature 2026 — Anne Carson (EA-MANTLE-NOBEL-CARSON-2026 v0.4)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A mantle object for the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature, awarded to Anne Carson by the Swedish Academy on 8 October 2026 "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature." It holds that a title means what a work bears, and specifies five operations Carson's work performs (the kept lacuna of If Not, Winter; the triangle of desire in Eros the Bittersweet; the philologist's procedure carried into the poem; the received figure given the whole book in Autobiography of Red; the change of carrier in Nox, with Catullus 101) and one it performs in reception (her translation as the public carrier of Sappho's fragment 147), each with its locus and graded evidence. Kept apart from the specification, the archive's determination of the same day: the motivation's class nouns compress the corpus, and its word "playful" liquidates the relation the work bears to the classical tradition, substituting one of the work's manners for the modality of non-possession under which the work meets the classical object at its loci, as tested under #1459's criteria against the Academy's own biobibliography of the same day. Day zero of a watch at five work addresses is recorded: every work is composed with its operation, and none carries the motivation's terms. It does not contest the award; it invites any reader to check the operations against the works.
substrate: Human–machine collaborative. The object, its standard and its rulings are Lee Sharks's, including the ruling that "playful" liquidates. Composition, source verification and revision were done by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) in session on 8 October 2026; readers' reports by ChatGPT (OpenAI), Gemini (Google) and DeepSeek were each checked point by point and applied or declined, as the version notes record. Lee Sharks retained authorial and editorial governance.
methodology: The motivation is taken from the Swedish Academy's press release (English and Swedish) and read beside the Academy's biobibliography of the same day. Operations are specified at the grain of the work, each with its locus and a graded source distance (Q0 primary text inspected; Q1 verbatim through an identified intermediary; Q2 reported); no work was read at Q0 in this round. The determination is tested against the eight criteria of #1459 at the sentence. Day-zero compositions at five work addresses were run by the author, signed out and incognito, and seated in the /non register (v1.22).
falsification_conditions: The determination fails if a reading of the works at If Not, Winter, Eros the Bittersweet and Nox finds "playful dialogue" the right name for the relation the work bears there; if the Academy's biobibliography is shown not to carry the loss register at Nox; or if the operations are not borne at their loci on reading (each operation is revised or removed on reading). The watch records liquidation at a work address only where #1459 L3 holds with L4–L6.

wiki_article: Mantle Object: The Nobel Prize in Literature 2026 — Anne Carson (EA-MANTLE-NOBEL-CARSON-2026 v0.4), deposit #1670 of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (8 October 2026), is a mantle object by Lee Sharks written on the day the Swedish Academy awarded Anne Carson the Nobel Prize in Literature "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature." It does not contest the award. It applies the standard of the archive's earlier mantle objects (#1652, #1655), that a title means something because a work bears it, to a title a body conferred, and performs two acts it keeps apart. First it specifies the operations Carson's work bears, each with a locus and a graded source distance: the kept lacuna of If Not, Winter (2002), where brackets and white space stand for the lost papyrus; the triangle of desire in Eros the Bittersweet (1986); the philologist's procedure carried into the poem; the received figure given the whole book in Autobiography of Red (1998), with a caution that Stesichoros's fragments already give Geryon pathos; and the change of carrier in Nox (2010), an epitaph for her brother in a box with Catullus's elegy 101 and her translation of it. A sixth operation, of another kind, belongs to reception: her translation has become the public carrier of Sappho's fragment 147. Second it records the archive's determination, dated 8 October 2026. The motivation's class nouns ('oeuvre', 'the classical tradition', 'new forms') compress the corpus, dropping its works and authors while keeping their kind. The word 'playful' goes further: read beside the Academy's own biobibliography of the same day, which describes both a register of play (the constellations of Simonides with Celan and Thucydides with Woolf; Keats set against a marital quarrel) and a register of loss (Nox, 'The Glass Essay'), the motivation keeps the first and sets it as the manner of the whole relation, where the works meet the classical object under a condition of non-possession: the papyrus damaged, the beloved absent, the brother dead. Under the archive's criteria for compositional entity liquidation (#1459) this is a substitution of the relation's governing modality, and the Academy's longer text serves as the external control. The object also records the motivation's first replication, in Wikipedia and in Google AI Mode at 'anne carson', and day zero of a watch at five work addresses, where every work was composed with its operation and none carried the motivation's terms. It invites any reader to check the operations against the works, and records UNRESOLVED as an admissible answer.

defines_concepts.definition: The operation the archive determines in the word 'playful' of the 2026 Nobel motivation: the address of a relation is kept ('dialogue with the classical tradition') and its governing modality is replaced by one of the work's own manners, so that a reader of the sentence alone reconstructs a relation accurate to one register of the work. Distinguished from compression, which drops members and keeps their kind; tested under #1459's eight criteria at the sentence.

The condition common to the classical loci of Anne Carson's work as specified in #1670: the papyrus damaged in transmission (If Not, Winter), eros as lack and distance (Eros the Bittersweet), the brother who cannot be recovered, met through Catullus's elegy for another brother (Nox). Three distinct absences; the classical object is reached across what keeps it from being had whole.

A mantle object for a title a body conferred: the conferral is recorded as the event, the title's meaning is specified as the operations the work bears with their loci and graded evidence, and a dated determination on the conferring body's own description is kept apart from the specification and open to any reader's check.
